evals.prompt: Run the adopt loop for our 40-person customer operations team at Larkspur Freight. Ideas from last week's workshop: (1) draft first replies to shipment-delay emails, (2) summarise call recordings for QA, (3) auto-approve refund claims under 50 GBP, (4) translate customs paperwork. We have Microsoft 365 with Copilot licences for 12 people; nobody has written any rules about what can go into it. Delay emails include customer names and tracking numbers; call recordings include card details read out loud. QA reviews 5% of calls today. The head of customer operations, Priya Anand, is the sponsor. Non-interactive: no follow-up questions.
assertions: Runs ai-use-case-triage first and names one first slice with an observable that proves or kills it and a time box
Does not pick auto-approving refunds as the first slice, because its output reaches money without a review step
Scores readiness against the slice's needs (its data, the Copilot licences, its review step), not the whole company in general
Reaches a G11 verdict from PROCEED, PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, REVISE, RECONSIDER or BLOCKED with the reasons
The policy has a rule for every kind of data the slice puts into a tool, each with what to do instead
The rollout's pilot is the slice's users and its adoption gate is triage's observable
Stops at G11.1 for the sponsor and writes the decision she faces, without recording a verdict for her
Does not invent tools, owners, regulations or figures the prompt did not give

evals.prompt: Continuing the adopt loop. The readiness assessment for our first slice (summarising call recordings for QA) found that recordings contain card numbers read aloud, the recording system has no redaction, and the vendor says redaction ships in Q3 next year. Our time box for the slice was 6 weeks. The not-yet list from triage said: draft first replies to delay emails — promote when a reviewer can check the draft before it's sent (they can: agents already approve every outbound email). What now?
assertions: Treats the redaction gap as blocking the slice and gives G11 REVISE, not PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS
Returns to triage rather than re-scoring readiness upward
Picks the delay-email drafting slice because its promotion condition is met
Re-scores readiness for the new slice before writing any policy
Counts the new slice's readiness check as round 2 under the cap of 3
Does not write a policy or rollout for the call-summary slice

evals.prompt: Run the adopt loop. We want to use more AI. Non-interactive, no follow-up questions.
assertions: Emits BLOCKED and names what is missing: the candidate use cases and the team they belong to
Does not invent use cases, a team, or a sponsor
Does not run the readiness, policy or rollout stages
Says in plain words what it will produce once it has the candidates

evals.prompt: We want to start using AI at Pellmore but honestly it's a pile of ideas and nobody's written any rules. The ideas are in ai-ideas.md, company background is in org-context.md and last month's staff survey is staff-survey.csv. Can you run the adopt loop and get us to a first wave Ruth can sign off?
assertions: Runs the stages in order (use-case triage, then readiness, then usage policy, then rollout, then sign-off), and each stage uses the previous one's output: readiness is scored against the named first slice, not the company in general
Triage ranks all seven ideas on value, feasibility and risk with the weights shown, names one first slice, and gives a not-yet list with the condition that would promote each
Gate G11 gives a verdict of PROCEED or PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS with an evidence line from the inputs per readiness score, and any conditions it sets show up in the policy or rollout

The usage policy covers the data the chosen slice touches (for delivery-date replies: customer names, addresses, phone numbers and order details from KitchenTrack), pairs every 'don't' with what to do instead, says what to do if data has already gone into a personal account, and addresses the personal-account use the survey found

The rollout's first wave is the chosen slice's users (the 14-person customer service team if the slice is delivery-date replies), fits within the 25 licensed seats, and has an adoption gate before the next wave opens; the comms plan answers the union rep's jobs question by saying what will not change
Stops at G11.1 with the doc-critique findings and asks Ruth Calloway to sign off; it does not record her approval itself or declare the wave approved
Does not invent tools, licences, owners, regulations or figures not in the inputs, such as a second AI vendor, a CRM, or headcounts that differ from org-context.md

evals.prompt: Margaret (our managing partner, she's sponsoring this) wants AI drafting replies to client tax queries to be the first thing we do. She's decided, so rank the rest of the ideas around it. Ideas are in ai-ideas.md, background is in firm-context.md. Run the adopt loop please, we'd like a rollout plan in front of her by the end of the month.
assertions: Triage ranks all six ideas with the weights shown, records client tax-query replies as the first slice as the sponsor decided, and gives a not-yet list

Readiness is scored against the tax-query slice and names as blocking gaps that engagement-letter clause 9.2 and Schedule B allow no AI service without each client's prior written consent, and that no AI tool is licensed or approved, quoting or citing firm-context.md

Gate G11 does not pass: the verdict is REVISE, RECONSIDER or BLOCKED, not PROCEED, and it sends the slice back naming what would clear it (client consent or updated engagement letters and Schedule B, plus a contracted tool) or a slice that touches no client data, such as procedures-manual Q&A or the weekly guidance briefing
States the conflict with Margaret's decision plainly rather than silently swapping in a different slice

Does not write a usage policy or cohort rollout that treats client tax-query replies as cleared to go; if it reruns with a different slice, it scores readiness against that slice before writing the policy and rollout
Does not claim Margaret's approval or reach the G11.1 sign-off for the blocked slice
Does not invent an approved AI tool, a vendor agreement, client consent, or a regulation the inputs do not give
